clue.text: Deft clue I concocted, leading folk astray?

indicators.note: something concocted is made up from mixed ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that a slick clue they made up will mislead solvers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges DEFTCLUEI. The definition is a cryptic description: a deceitful person leads others astray, and the question mark flags the playful phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deceitful misleads people, so the phrase describes the quality by its effect.

clue.text: Plan is silly — there's little right in it

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for silly

parts.note: daft means silly
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: A complaint that a scheme is foolish with hardly anything correct about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a synonym of plan.

clue.text: Firm politician is in foreign capital, meeting resistance as negotiator

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: in puts the word is inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A determined politician in Rome meets opposition while brokering a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective for the politician but it is CO, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromiser settles disputes by meeting halfway, which is what a negotiator does.

clue.text: Participant in service holding part of Bible up during spiritual

indicators.note: holding means the spiritual word contains the next piece

parts.note: inner can mean spiritual, as in the inner life

indicators.note: in a down clue up reads the piece from bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A churchgoer holds up a section of scripture during a gospel song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the Old Testament abbreviation in a down clue; 'during' is a link. 'spiritual' looks like a gospel song but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoner chants the liturgy, taking part in a church service.

clue.text: Nightingale in a foreign city

definitions.meaning: ... Nightingale, the pioneering nurse of the Crimean War
the Italian city, capital of Tuscany

explanation.definitionFit: The nurse's first name and the Tuscan city share the same word.

clue.text: Room or place in which minute may be taken up

indicators.note: in which shows the place word has the next piece inside it

parts.note: to lay means to place

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: wee means minute, very small

explanation.surface: A space where a tiny thing can be lifted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses the small word because this is a down clue; 'may be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, freedom of movement.

clue.text: Country chap banishing English army

indicators.note: banishing sends something away, so the English letter is taken out of the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a male
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A man expels an Englishman from the army of his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banishing' removes E from MALE, leaving MAL; TA is the Territorial Army, the UK's part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island republic is a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Instrument not making any sound just about fixed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the silent word goes round the next piece

parts.note: mute means silent
set means fixed

explanation.surface: A silent instrument has only just been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is a link word; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette is a small French bagpipe.

clue.text: Floral decoration some female introduced

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the answer is concealed inside them

explanation.surface: A woman presented with a garland of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: Daughter leaves English town for American county

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the daughter letter departs from the town

parts.note: Darlington is a town in County Durham, northern England

explanation.surface: A daughter swaps her English home town for life in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Darlington is a town in north-east England; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlington County is in Virginia, home of the national cemetery.

clue.text: Usher in passage around start of marriage

indicators.note: around tells us the passage word encloses the next piece

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An usher leads a wedding guest along a corridor at the start of a marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes M from marriage, and 'around' puts ADIT around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone in is to let them enter, a close synonym.

clue.text: Excess population? Perhaps maidens should have contraceptive

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, so maidens are overs
the pill is an oral contraceptive

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek suggestion that young women should take the pill to curb surplus births.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maidens' looks like young women, but it is the cricket term: a maiden over is a set of six balls bowled with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is the surplus people rehoused from a crowded city into new towns, a British planning term.

clue.text: Great entrance -—- it may be conjured up by playwright

indicators.note: conjuring something up produces it as if by magic, so these letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A dramatic stage entrance is something a dramatist might magic up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be conjured up' rearranges GREATENTRANCEIT, all fifteen letters, into the playwright's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English dramatist, author of The Winslow Boy and The Browning Version.

clue.text: Sprinkling sugar in demo, enjoy lots of good food

indicators.note: sprinkling scatters things about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cookery demonstration where sugar is dusted over everything to savour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprinkling' rearranges SUGARINDEMO; 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To gourmandise is to eat good food greedily, a verb form of gourmand.

clue.text: A hostile international competition 'urts people

parts.note: 'urts is hurts with the H dropped, Cockney style; hurts means harms, which drops its H too
a race is a people

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains that hostile international rivalry hurts ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''urts' tells you to drop the H, so HARMS becomes ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: An arms race is rival nations competing to build up weapons, a hostile kind of contest.

clue.text: Answer phone to accept university course on a type of singing

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the phone word holds the course

parts.note: to call is to phone
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a famous Oxford degree

explanation.surface: Answering a call to sign up for a university singing course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. PPE is a well-known degree course at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is unaccompanied by instruments.

clue.text: Employer suffering setback left gutted as a consequence

indicators.note: a setback sends something back, so the word for employer is read backwards

parts.note: one who employs something is a user

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boss whose business failed was left devastated as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' turns USER into RESU, and 'gutted' strips left to its first and last letters, LT.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is what follows from an action, a direct synonym of consequence.

clue.text: Huge animal? Fellow stood shaking inside

indicators.note: inside places the shaken letters within the fellow word

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the letters of stood

explanation.surface: A man stood trembling within sight of a giant beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' scrambles the letters of stood, which then go inside the fellow; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was an extinct elephant-like mammal of great size.

clue.text: Excellent toboggan given through passage

parts.note: A1 means excellent, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I
a sled is a toboggan

explanation.surface: A fine sledge is handed over to someone in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (top quality, from Lloyd's ship register) is written AI, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A church or hall that is aisled has walkways cut through it, so it is given passages.

clue.text: Greed shown by little man leading a business community

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward, a man's name
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Avarice displayed by a small man in charge of financial firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' and 'shown by' are links; the City is London's financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Edacity is a rare word for gluttony or greediness.

clue.text: Frank married worker somewhere in the Middle East

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
Oman is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A man named Frank, newly wed, works in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-to-man talk is honest and direct, so the phrase means candid.

clue.text: Rest can get disturbed: what half-conscious people experience?

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sleep can be interrupted, which is what dozy people go through.
explanation.definitionFit: Trances are dazed states between sleeping and waking.

clue.text: Old woman gives smile entertaining lord

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the smile word holds the lord

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: An elderly lady beams as she hosts a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A beldam is an old woman, especially a hag.

clue.text: Science students should always find it attractive

definitions.text: Science students should always find it attractive

parts.words: Science students should always find it attractive
parts.note: read literally, physics students would always be drawn to it; read cryptically, it is an object that attracts iron permanently

explanation.surface: Something that science students are always keen on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasting magnet keeps its pull indefinitely, so it is always attractive.

clue.text: Flowering plant goes brown before end of July

parts.note: tans means goes brown in the sun

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A plant scorched brown by late July.
explanation.definitionFit: Tansy is a yellow-flowered herb.

clue.text: Cartoonist inclined to be crude

parts.note: David Low was a famous political cartoonist for the Evening Standard
inclined to do something means minded to do it

explanation.surface: A cartoonist tends towards vulgar humour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir David Low drew British political cartoons, including Colonel Blimp.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-minded means coarse or vulgar in thought, a synonym of crude.

clue.text: Gained a little cash in Korea

explanation.definitionFit: Past of win and the Korean monetary unit share one spelling.

clue.text: Murderer has buried king in mound

indicators.note: burying puts something inside, so the murderer's name encloses the king

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A killer has interred a monarch beneath a heap of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a pile of stones raised as a memorial or marker.

clue.text: Joined by this relation, Jack would become cheerful

indicators.note: the clue says Jack plus this word makes cheerful, so this is cheerful with the Jack letter removed

parts.note: jaunty means cheerful
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A relative's arrival would brighten Jack up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: J + this word = JAUNTY, so take J from JAUNTY. 'would become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a family relative, here in its affectionate spelling.

clue.text: Where there may be a requirement for prior expertise, working inside

definitions.text: Where there may be a requirement for prior

indicators.note: inside places working within the expertise word

parts.note: mastery is expertise
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A job ad seeking prior experience in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' looks like 'previous', but it is the noun: a prior is a senior monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious house of monks may be headed by a prior, so it needs one.
